The representation is implemented as either a neural implicit model conditioned on a time variable, a set of 3D Gaussians with time-dependent parameters, or an explicit feature grid [S1].

The claim lists three specific implementation forms: 1) a neural implicit model conditioned on a time variable, 2) a set of 3D Gaussians with time-dependent parameters, and 3) an explicit feature grid. The evidence explicitly supports the first two forms in Section 6.2 ('A neural implicit model conditioned on a time variable' and 'A set of 3D Gaussians shared across frames, where time-dependent parameters encode motion'). However, regarding the third form, the evidence states that the *encoding function* can be an 'explicit feature grid' (Section 6.2) and that Section 6.3 discusses 'Feature-grid encoding for dynamic representations' as a way to accelerate optimization, but it does not explicitly list 'an explicit feature grid' as a primary form of the space-time representation alongside the neural implicit model and 3D Gaussians in the same list. More critically, the claim implies these are the three main forms of the representation itself, whereas the text distinguishes between the representation function (which can be implicit or Gaussian) and the encoding mechanism (which can be an MLP or feature grid). While related, the text does not support the claim that 'an explicit feature grid' is a representation form on par with the other two in the same categorical list provided in the text. The text lists the first two as forms of the unified function, and the feature grid as an alternative encoding strategy or acceleration method. Therefore, not every fact in the claim is directly supported as a primary representation form in the evidence.
